title: Enhanced derived adjunction and monoidal Quillen calculus
statement:
Here a combinatorial differential graded model category means a locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups (with cochain differentials and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, closure under retracts, and functorial factorizations into (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), with the corresponding lifting properties. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Enrichment satisfies the model compatibility axiom: for a cofibration $i$ and a fibration $p$, the induced map of Hom complexes is a fibration in the projective model structure on complexes of abelian groups, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is trivial. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. Stable means that the enhanced localization has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its homotopy pushout squares are exactly its homotopy pullback squares. A differential graded Quillen adjunction is an enriched adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Its enhanced localization retains derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies; equivalently one may use the associated stable homotopy theory with its chain enrichment when the model category is stable.

For stable combinatorial differential graded model categories $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ and a differential graded Quillen adjunction $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$, the enhanced localizations have derived functors $\mathbf L L$ and $\mathbf R R$ and a natural equivalence of derived mapping complexes
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(\mathbf L L X,Y)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,\mathbf R R Y).$$
The unit and counit are enhanced natural transformations satisfying the triangle identities with their coherence homotopies. The equivalence sends $h$ to $\mathbf R R(h)\eta_X$ and has inverse $g\mapsto\epsilon_Y\mathbf L L(g)$. Functorial cofibrant and fibrant replacements present these constructions. Composition of left Quillen functors and composition of right Quillen functors admit coherent derived composition identifications; enriched natural transformations between such functors induce enhanced derived transformations by evaluating on the appropriate replacements. Objectwise weak-equivalence transformations on these replacements induce equivalences. Strict enriched composition, identity and naturality diagrams thereby give coherent diagrams after localization. A functor already preserving weak equivalences has the enhancement induced directly by localization.

The same assertion holds in several variables for an enriched left Quillen bifunctor, meaning a two-variable left adjoint whose pushout product preserves cofibrations and is trivial if either input cofibration is trivial. In particular a closed symmetric monoidal differential graded model category has enhanced derived tensor, internal Hom and tensor-Hom evaluation, with coherent associativity, symmetry and unit maps induced from its monoidal model structure. Strong monoidal left Quillen functors induce coherent strong monoidal derived functors. For enhanced functors obtained this way, the unit/composition/counit formula defining an adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] defines an enhanced transformation, and mate formation respects coherent composition diagrams. This asserts functoriality for the specified enriched data, not a lifting of arbitrary transformations supplied only on ordinary homotopy categories.
